learningObjective: Understand ONNX's operator set and opset versioning model.
stem: Which statement about ONNX opsets is correct?

options.text: ONNX opsets are monotonically merged over time: a runtime supporting opset 18 automatically supports the exact semantics of every opset from 1 to 17 without any per-version handling.
ONNX opsets are only a display feature; every ONNX runtime implements the union of all opset versions simultaneously, so opset numbers can be ignored.

An ONNX model declares a specific opset version (e.g., `opset_import: [domain="", version=17]`); each op's semantics is defined by the version listed in that opset, and consumers must implement the exact opset version to execute the model correctly.
The opset version determines only the file-format layout on disk; the operator semantics themselves never change across versions.

explanation: ONNX uses opset versioning to snapshot op semantics: each model declares which opset version(s) it uses (via `opset_import` in the model proto), and consumers must implement that specific opset. Op semantics can change across opset versions (new attributes, new ops, retirement/deprecation of old ops), so runtimes typically implement multiple opsets and dispatch based on the model's declared version. This is what makes ONNX a stable interchange format across framework/runtime versions.

optionExplanations.C: Correct: opset versioning is the semantic snapshot mechanism.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: opsets are semantic, not display-only.
optionExplanations.A: Wrong: version-specific semantics differ; automatic union is not the model.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: op semantics do evolve across opsets.

assumptions: ONNX specification as of 2026; opset versioning is stable across recent revisions.
nonImplications: Does not imply every runtime must support every opset; converters and shape inference tools bridge gaps.
Does not imply an opset is a whole-model version; each domain has its own opset.

distractorRationales.A: Wrong claim of automatic version union.
distractorRationales.D: Confuses format layout with op semantics.
